JYOTI CNC Q2 FY27: ₹5,082 CR ORDER BOOK; ₹1,020.65 CR INVESTMENT APPROVED UNDER ECMS, 10,000 MACHINES CAPACITY EXPANSION & RECORD DISPATCHES

• ECMS Investment Approval: Received approval for ₹1,020.65 Cr investment over five years at its Rajkot facility under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme, eligible for up to 25% capital subsidy

• Additional Subsidy: Applied for matching subsidy under the Gujarat Government scheme, offering potential additional financial support for expansion

• Capacity Expansion: Existing Indian manufacturing capacity of 6,000 machines annually, with additional 10,000 machines per year capacity being brought into use

• Foundry Expansion: Newly developed foundry operations expected to commence shortly, supporting backward integration and manufacturing efficiency

• Record Order Book: Outstanding order book reached ₹5,082 Cr as of September 2026, supported by strong demand across aerospace, defence, automobile and engineering sectors

• Q2 Order Inflows: Secured ₹809 Cr new orders during Q2 FY27, while orders worth ₹575 Cr were executed

• Record Dispatches: Dispatched 1,900 CNC machines during Q2 FY27, highest-ever quarterly dispatches, with management optimistic about sustaining momentum

• Aerospace & Defence Business: Contributed 36% of total order book, reflecting significant exposure to high-precision machine requirements

• Automobile Business: Contributed 22% of order book, while general engineering accounted for 21%, supporting diversified future execution

• Cash Flow Improvement: H1 consolidated operating cash flow surged to ₹111.7 Cr from ₹13.2 Cr YoY, with OCF-to-EBITDA conversion improving to approximately 47% from 6%

• New Product Development: Introduced advanced CNC machines including MTX 100, GU 8, HP 4000/6000 and Tachyon Beta, targeting aerospace, defence, automotive, EV and electronics manufacturing

• Manufacturing Automation: Continued investment in in-house R&D, AI-enabled machine safety, automation and high-precision machining to strengthen product competitiveness

• Future Growth Strategy: Focused on aerospace and defence, EVs, semiconductors, electronics manufacturing services and higher-end CNC machines

• FY27 Guidance & Capex: Management disclosed the five-year ECMS investment approval and manufacturing expansion plans

GLOBAL SURFACES Q2 FY27: EBITDA TURNS POSITIVE AT ₹1.3 CR; REVENUE UP 11% YOY, UAE EXPANSION & DOMESTIC SALES INITIATED

• H2 FY27 Outlook: Management focusing on improving operating efficiency, expanding domestic sales, diversifying export markets and managing elevated input costs

• Domestic Market Expansion: Commenced domestic dispatches in India from October 2026, supported by an expanded marketing team to reduce dependence on exports

• UAE Business Expansion: Plans to strengthen local market presence in the UAE by leveraging its existing Dubai manufacturing facility and regional distribution infrastructure

• Dubai Capacity: Operates an engineered quartz manufacturing facility with 6,22,895 square metres annual production capacity, supporting exports to international markets

• India Manufacturing: Jaipur facility has annual engineered stone capacity of 5,21,454 square metres, taking combined production capacity to approximately 11.44 lakh square metres

• Export Business: Exports contributed approximately 96% of H1 FY27 revenue, highlighting the company's significant dependence on overseas markets

• Premium Product Expansion: Focused on scaling Marquartz, a patented premium engineered quartz product designed to replicate natural marble and granite patterns

• Technology Partnership: Dubai subsidiary holds exclusive licensed manufacturing rights for certain patented engineered quartz technologies in the MENA region, with first right of refusal in India

• Raw Material Pressure: Input costs increased 25–50%, while imported freight costs rose nearly fivefold, affecting operating profitability

• Forex Impact: Lower unrealised foreign exchange gains contributed to weaker reported profitability compared with the previous year

• Capital Restructuring: Board approved conversion of an additional ₹110.44 Cr unsecured loans into equity of Dubai subsidiary Global Surfaces FZE, subject to completion of regulatory formalities

• Natural Stone Business: Discontinued operations at its Jaipur natural stone manufacturing unit effective March 31, 2026, to focus on engineered quartz

• H1 Performance: Revenue declined 2.6% YoY to ₹125.3 Cr, while EBITDA increased to ₹9.6 Cr from ₹4.4 Cr YoY; net loss stood at ₹5.3 Cr versus ₹5.1 Cr YoY

• H1 Margin Recovery: EBITDA margin improved to 7.66% from 3.42% YoY, although profitability remained negative at the net level

• Debt Position: Debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.58x, while total borrowings declined to approximately ₹155.4 Cr from ₹163.3 Cr in March 2026

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on premium quartz products, expanding US and UAE distribution, increasing domestic penetration, optimising sourcing and improving manufacturing profitability

MMP INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: PAT UP 73% YOY; 18,000 MTPA WIRE ROD PLANT TARGETED IN Q4 FY27, H2 CABLE REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE AT 40–50%

• H2 FY27 Revenue Guidance: Management expects Aluminium Conductors & Cables revenue to grow 40–50% in H2 FY27 compared with H1 FY27, supported by recovery in project execution

• Quarterly Results: Revenue increased 35% YoY and 9% QoQ to ₹252.7 Cr, while EBITDA grew 44% YoY but declined 8% QoQ to ₹19.3 Cr

• Profitability: PAT surged 73% YoY to ₹12.1 Cr but declined 12% QoQ, impacted by inventory valuation losses and higher input costs

• Margin Performance: EBITDA margin improved to 7.6% from 7.1% YoY but declined from 9% QoQ

• Wire Rod Capacity Expansion: New 18,000 MTPA aluminium wire rod manufacturing facility at an advanced stage, targeting commercial production in Q4 FY27

• LT Cable Expansion: Additional 6,000 MTPA low-tension power cable capacity under development, with trial production targeted for Q4 FY28

• New Product Launches: Security Printing Foil and Lidding Foil launches targeted in Q3 FY27; manufacturing line ready with initial trials completed

• LT Cable Commercialisation: Received BIS certification, with utility approvals progressing; commercial sales expected to gain momentum from Q4 FY27

• Aluminium Powder Business: Revenue increased 37% YoY to ₹161 Cr, supported by strong domestic demand and record export order execution

• Aluminium Foil Business: Revenue surged 47% YoY to ₹75 Cr, supported by strong demand across bare and printed foils

• Conductors & Cables: Revenue declined 16% YoY to ₹16 Cr due to monsoon-related project delays; management expects a stronger H2 recovery

• Polymer Insulator Expansion: Developed products up to 765 kV, with 10 lakh units annual manufacturing capacity and ₹35–40 Cr already invested

• Polymer Insulator Orders: Secured export orders from Latin America and South Asia, while additional domestic utility approvals remain under process

• Solar Capex: ₹30 Cr investment planned for approximately 7 MW captive solar capacity; plant ready but commissioning delayed due to regulatory approvals

• Renewable Energy Target: Plans to increase renewable energy contribution from approximately 20% to 35–40% over the next 3–4 years

• Advanced Aluminium Powders: Developing specialised high-value aluminium powders in collaboration with ISRO, targeting improved product mix and realisations

• Star Circlips Expansion: Associate company expects record H2 FY27 sales, with fine-blanking products contributing from Q4 FY27 and a new hot-forging facility targeted for Q1 FY28

• H1 Performance: Revenue increased 31% YoY to ₹485.3 Cr, EBITDA grew 52% to ₹40.3 Cr and PAT reached ₹25.8 Cr versus ₹1.6 Cr YoY, aided by a low base following the Q1 FY26 fire incident

• Future Growth Strategy: Focused on export expansion, backward integration, value-added aluminium products, power cables, polymer insulators and lowering manufacturing costs

• FY27 Consolidated Guidance: No quantified company-wide revenue growth, EBITDA margin or total capex guidance disclosed

India’s Furniture QCO amendment provides conditional relief for qualifying furniture shipments — including imports from China!

Under the Furniture (Quality Control) Third Amendment Order, 2026, dated 2 November 2026, imports are exempt under this provision when ALL THREE deadlines are met:

✅ Purchase Order placed on or before 12 August 2026
✅ Bill of Lading issued on or before 30 November 2026
✅ Bill of Entry issued on or before 31 December 2026

📄 Importers must submit copies of these documents, along with other supporting documents, to BIS within SEVEN DAYS of consignment clearance. The submission must be on the importer’s letterhead and duly signed by its authorised signatory.

📌 Relief applies only to shipments meeting every condition. New purchase orders placed after 12 August 2026 do not qualify under this provision.

Importers sourcing furniture from Guangzhou, Foshan and across China — check your documents and plan your shipments within these deadlines!

Srinibas Pradhan Constructions Limited: Rising Infrastructure Investments to Support Growth Opportunities in Eastern India

Srinibas Pradhan Constructions Limited stands to benefit from increasing investments in district roads, rural bridges and railway infrastructure, with government spending strengthening connectivity and creating opportunities for regional infrastructure contractors.

Key Highlights:
* Infrastructure Spending: Odisha allocates 7.5% of its budget to roads and bridges, compared with the 4.3% average across 31 states.
* Government Investment: Over ₹32,000 Cr approved for rural roads and bridges over five years, including ₹11,800 Cr for the Setu Bandhan programme.
* Railway Infrastructure: Odisha received ₹10,928 Cr for railways in Union Budget FY27, with approximately ₹90,659 Cr of projects underway.
* Business Development: Subsidiary emerged as L1 bidder for a ₹30.81 Cr PWD Odisha road project under CRIF in Jharsuguda.
* Improved Work Classification: Upgraded to Class A in FY26

Rising infrastructure spending, improved contractor classifications and a growing share of direct government and PSU business could strengthen the company's positioning for upcoming infrastructure opportunities in Eastern India.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
